stories.title: What happens when a bank ducks rules in Pakistan? For Deutsche Bank, perhaps nothing
summary: Yet, even as policymakers were scrambling to bolster the defences of the nation’s financial system, vulnerabilities in the internal systems of Deutsche Bank’s Pakistan operations were complicating the fight against illicit money flows.

Local compliance challenges In October 2019, the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) introduced key requirements under its Trade-Based Money Laundering (TBML) framework and ordered banks to implement them with immediate effect.

Confusion over KYC function In September 2019, Chiara Monaco from the anti-financial crime unit at Deutsche Bank’s headquarters in Frankfurt emailed bank staff in Pakistan to flag a concern regarding “certain sub-accounts in Pakistan belonging to customers not KYC’ed”.

stories.title: 'Pakistani flag rises into orbit' as Zeeshan Ali makes history aboard China's Shenzhou-24 spacecraft
summary: Forty-year-old Zeeshan Ali became the first Pakistani astronaut to enter orbit on Wednesday, after China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft entered its preset orbit following liftoff from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre.
The China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) said the crew will conduct around 90 experiments during the mission.

Pakistan’s space agency Suparco and CMSA signed a cooperation agreement in February 2025, under which two Pakistanis were to train in China, with one joining a mission on the Tiangong space station operated by Beijing.

stories.title: Pakistan Customs seizes nearly 1kg of 'Multan-bound' marijuana in Karachi
summary: The Collectorate of Customs (CoC) (airports) in Karachi foiled a narcotics smuggling attempt and seized 900 grams of marijuana during routine scanning at the International Mail Office (IMO), Pakistan Customs said on Tuesday.
During routine scanning, Customs staff intercepted a “suspicious parcel” originating from Canada’s Ontario and destined for Multan, the statement said. “The parcel was declared as ‘Books (Gift)’.
The seized marijuana was valued at approximately Rs27.25 million, Pakistan Customs said.

stories.title: Cabinet approves deregulation of sugar sector to meet vital IMF benchmark
summary: ISLAMABAD: To meet a long-postponed structural benchmark of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the federal cabinet on Tuesday approved the deregulation of the sugar sector, an end to its export subsidies and free movement among the provinces.
The IMF has continuously pushed for a policy ending the government’s role in sugar sector operations, from sugarcane crop prices to sugar production and import-export, leaving it to market forces.

The policy, nevertheless, retains the government’s right to maintain buffer sugar stocks and take measures to access correct and timely information on sugarcane crop, sugar production and market availability.

stories.title: 11 injured as Riyadh skyscraper hit second time in less than a week
summary: Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence reported Tuesday’s injuries and posted a picture of the landmark tower housing the headquarters of the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF).

The Houthis, who control much of western Yemen including the capital Sanaa, have been firing at Saudi airports, oil infrastructure and office buildings since Yemen’s frozen civil war reignited in July in a knock-on from the US-Iran war.
The Saudi-led coalition intervened in Yemen in early 2015, after the Houthis had captured the capital Sanaa and sent the internationally recognised government fleeing to Aden.

stories.title: Huang’s return fails to dispel doubts as Nvidia shares drop
summary: Technology shares led a market retreat on Tuesday as caution returned after Jensen Huang’s extraordinary return to AI giant Nvidia days after he was forced to resign, with investors bracing for further volatility in a key sector driving economic growth worldwide.

A day after Huang’s reinstatement as CEO drove Nvidia shares up more than 30 per cent, adding more than $900 billion to the firm’s market value, the euphoria dissipated as its stock lost almost 9pc mid-session.

But “Jensen Huang alone cannot support the AI trade in the long term,” said Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB. “Nvidia’s stock price decline on Tuesday is to be expected after such a large rally in the previous session,” she added.

stories.title: Islamabad United snap up Matt Henry, Karachi Kings secure Adil Rashid as direct signings for PSL 12
summary: Islamabad United have signed New Zealand fast bowler Matt Henry, while Karachi Kings have secured the services of England leg-spinner Adil Rashid as their marquee direct signings for the 12th edition of the Pakistan Super League (PSL).
Multan Sultans have also utilised the direct-signing facility, bringing Australian fast bowler Lance Morris on board ahead of the player auction scheduled for January 23, 2027.

The direct-signing window, which opened on October 23 and closed on November 23, allowed each of the eight franchises to recruit one overseas marquee player who did not feature in either PSL 10 or PSL 11.

stories.title: PTI moves IHC for live broadcast of Al-Qadir Trust case hearing
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) has filed a petition in the Islamabad High Court (IHC), seeking live broadcast of the appeal proceedings in the £190 million Al-Qadir Trust case involving party founder Imran Khan.

It argues that the case is a matter of national importance and that live broadcasting of Imran’s appeal proceedings is essential to ensure transparency, uphold justice and maintain public confidence in the judicial system.

The petition argues that live broadcasting would allow an independent assessment of all legal aspects of the case and requested the IHC to order the live broadcast of the complete proceedings of the appeal.

stories.title: Rohail Nazir's fifty books Asia Cup Rising Stars semi-finals spot for Pakistan Shaheens
summary: An unbeaten half-century by Rohail Nazir, followed by a devastating bowling display, helped Pakistan Shaheens defeat Nepal by 96 runs in their final Group ‘B’ match of the Asia Cup Rising Stars at the University of Doha for Science and Technology on Tuesday.
Batting first, Pakistan Shaheens were in trouble at 66-6 in 16.5 overs before wicket-keeper-batter Rohail steadied the innings with an unbeaten 64 off 83 balls, hitting four fours and three sixes.
Hasnain and Sufyan took three wickets each for 21 and 17 runs respectively, while Imran claimed two for 29.

stories.title: Fazl decries ‘state siege’, claims prevented from attending Lahore event
summary: LAHORE: Police began removing barriers around Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s place of stay in Lahore on Tuesday evening, with the Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief claiming he had been put under an hours-long “state siege” to restrict his movement.

In an earlier video message, the JUI-F chief alleged that he was under a “state siege” and that roadblocks and checkpoints across Lahore were preventing him from attending a multi-party seminar organised by the LHCBA.

In a statement, the party’s spokesperson warned that arrests of JUI-F workers in different cities on Monday, followed by the alleged deployment of a heavy police contingent outside the party chief’s residence, would have political consequences for the government.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz assures KP governor of continued support to eliminate terrorism
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday assured KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi of all possible cooperation on behalf of the federal government for the complete eradication of terrorism, durable peace and the welfare of the public in the province.
The federal government would continue to “fully support the implementation of the decisions taken at the apex committee meeting to completely eliminate terrorism”, he was quoted as saying.

He reaffirmed the federal government’s commitment to providing full support for the development of KP and the welfare of its people, saying that all possible resources would be mobilised to provide them with healthcare, education and other basic facilities, according to the PMO.

stories.title: Govt selects consortium of 3 foreign banks for $500m finance facility backed by MIGA
summary: According to the ministry, the decision was taken in a virtual meeting held by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb with the senior leadership of a consortium of international banks and representatives of the agency.

The banks were selected on the basis of the most competitive financing terms offered to the government, it said. “The one-year facility, renewable on a rolling 1+1+1 basis, will support the financing of essential imports and trade-related expenditures,” the statement said.

The ministry said the government would work closely with MIGA and the selected banks to advance the transaction towards its timely execution, looking forward to building strong and lasting relationships.

stories.title: 14 areas picked to boost shrimp farming
summary: He stated this while chairing a meeting of the Prime Minister's Sub-Committee on Crop Cluster Value Chain for Aqua Shrimp, constituted to develop the sector through coordinated efforts involving federal and provincial governments, industry and other stakeholders.
The sub-committee is working on a comprehensive strategy to address challenges and explore opportunities across the shrimp farming value chain.
The minister said all seven working groups had completed their meetings, with participation from provincial governments, industry representatives and relevant federal institutions.

stories.title: PSX rises 1,068 points in oil-driven rally
summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) extended gains on Tuesday, as investors drew confidence from a strong recovery in global equities and falling international oil prices, while buying across major sectors kept the market positive throughout the session.

Meanwhile, declining international oil prices, with Brent crude trading below $90 per barrel, provided an additional boost to market sentiment, particularly amid expectations of easing external-sector pressures.

"Going forward, the market is expected to maintain a positive bias, supported by declining international oil prices, improving investor sentiment and corporate-led catalysts, particularly ENGROH's share buyback announcement," Najib added.

stories.title: FoodAg 2026 generates $658m in expected business
summary: Over the first two days, more than 4,000 B2B meetings were held across key sectors such as rice, processed food, seafood, meat, cereals and oilseeds.

Further partnerships were forged in the seafood, rice, spices, salt, processed food and distribution sectors, connecting Pakistani companies with partners from China, the United Kingdom, Vietnam and Bangladesh.
Chief Executive TDAP Faiz Ahmad and Secretary TDAP Sheryar Taj met delegations from the European Union, China, Malaysia, Saudi Arabia and Kenya.

stories.title: Cybersecurity key to achieving Digital Pakistan vision
summary: Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja has said that cybersecurity is fundamental to the vision of Digital Pakistan, national security, and the protection of digital economy.

Highlighting three fundamental priorities for cybersecurity, the federal minister said that the first priority was the protection of cryptographic keys used in digital systems and preparedness to address future threats.

The plan includes the implementation of the Pakistan Information Security Framework at federal and provincial levels, the establishment of provincial and sectoral CERTs under National CERT, and the preparation of a National Cybersecurity Handbook for government officials.

stories.title: Planning Commission restructured
summary: The federal cabinet has approved a resolution for the Planning Commission restructuring, dividing its functions between a new policy wing and a development and analysis wing.
The Planning Commission would "act as the principal forum for economic decision making", said the resolution approved by the cabinet.
The commission would serve as an apex body for planning, policy coordination and implementation oversight to ensure sustained, sustainable and equitable socio-economic development, it added.

stories.title: Media monitor launches campaign to 'raise better sons' in effort to combat gender-based violence
summary: They were paid less than men,” Dr Tauseef pointed out, while talking about enlightened countries and societies which saw women at par with men and how quickly they developed.
The Uks director also pointed out that one thing ingrained in boys from childhood was that they were not supposed to cry. “If crying is only for women, then how come men have tear glands?

Senior journalist and activist Sohail Sangi said that there had been different attitudes towards women through the ages. “Behaviours and attitudes have changed with religions and regions,” he said. “I hail from Tharparkar where we had not even heard of things such as ‘karo kari’.

stories.title: Reacting to Bilawal's remarks on 'brute majority', a section of legal community wants 26th, 27th Amendments repealed
summary: In an open letter on Tuesday, 100 individuals — mostly lawyers and also including activists and academics — called for both the 26th and 27th Amendments to be repealed. “Pakistan’s constitutional order belongs to its people.
The 26th Amendment carved a constitutional bench out of the SC, with its members chosen by a reconstituted Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) in which judges no longer held a majority.

However, a majority “made up with seats that were unjustly denied to the opposition is not the majority the Constitution demands”, they contended. “An amendment passed on that basis holds no constitutional, legal, or democratic validity.

stories.title: Punjab Assembly adopts resolution seeking tougher punishment for blasphemy
summary: LAHORE: The Punjab Assembly on Tuesday unanimously passed a resolution demanding legislation to make the punishment harsher under Section 298-A (use of derogatory remarks, etc, in respect of holy personages) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC).
The House urged the federal government to move on the matter on a “priority basis” and enact legislation needed to increase the penalty under Section 298-A.
In August 2023, Parliament passed the Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill 2023 to increase the punishment under Section 298-A from three years of imprisonment to at least 10 years in jail.

stories.title: US envoy 'not certain' military aid to Israel will end this year as Trump promised
summary: US Ambassador to Israel ‌Mike Huckabee has cast doubt on whether Washington would end its $3.8 billion in annual military aid to Israel by the end of this year, as promised by President Donald Trump on the day of this month's midterm elections.

In his surprise announcement as voters headed to ​the polls on November 3, Trump said he had made a deal with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ​several months earlier to stop providing Israel with around $4 billion in annual US funding.
The election that day subsequently saw Democrats, including many who publicly oppose military funding for Israel, win ​control of both houses of Congress from Trump's Republicans.

stories.title: US Army sergeant pleads guilty to selling defence secrets to China
summary: Zhao provided excerpts from High Mobility Artillery Rocket System manuals, photographed restricted presentations on missile systems and exercises, and sold military computers and hard drives for thousands of dollars.
Agents arrested Zhao on March 6, 2025, seizing $30,000 in cash and multiple army hard drives.
Zhao faces up to 10 years in prison and a $250,000 fine at his March 1, 2027 sentencing.

stories.title: Five Turkish soldiers killed in helicopter crash, ministry says
summary: Five ‌Turkish soldiers were killed in ​a ​military helicopter crash ⁠in Turkey's ​central Eskisehir ​province on Tuesday, the Turkish Defence ​Ministry ​said.
"An AS-532 helicopter belonging to our Air Force crashed after taking off from Eskisehir for training purposes," the Turkish National Defense Ministry said in a statement.
"Five heroic comrades-in-arms serving aboard the helicopter belonging to our Air Force, which crashed during a training flight in Eskisehir, have been martyred," the statement said.

stories.title: Hours-long road closures around Karachi’s PIDC junction cause traffic congestion
summary: KARACHI: Commuters in Karachi’s Saddar area faced traffic congestion on Tuesday after authorities closed some roads around the PIDC junction for a few hours in response to a sit-in call by the Sindh Indus Lawyers Forum (SILF).
In an alert issued at 1:16pm, Karachi Traffic Police said both roads from PIDC Chowk towards the State Life Building, as well as Dr Ziauddin Ahmed Road, were closed to traffic.
In an update at around 6pm, the traffic police said the cut from PIDC Chowk towards State Life Building and both sides of Dr Ziauddin Ahmed Road have been reopened to commuters.

stories.title: Khawaja Asif optimistic about referendum on creation of new provinces early next year
summary: Asif criticised the threatening tone adopted by Naqvi towards Sanaullah, saying such remarks were inappropriate for political discourse. “I use very harsh language, and harsh language is also used against me, but threatening someone is not political language,” he said.

The proposal has drawn differing responses from political parties, with the PPP strongly opposing any move to divide Sindh, while the MQM-P has continued to advocate the creation of additional provinces, particularly in the province.
Meanwhile, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has supported the idea of creating as many as 12 provinces, arguing that smaller administrative units could improve governance and service delivery.

stories.title: Astronomers spot record-setting quasar in the early universe
summary: A supermassive black ​hole that powers a quasar is typically billions of times more massive than the sun.

The supermassive black hole ​powering this quasar had already grown to an ​enormous mass in an extremely short time, ⁠which challenges our understanding of how black holes can grow so large so quickly in the early universe," Belladitta said.
That gas can build up a single enormous star that quickly collapses into a black hole.

stories.title: Microsoft declares 'Code Red' after historic outage, internal memos show
summary: Microsoft has declared a "Code Red" drive to overhaul how it prevents and responds to major service failures after a 24-hour outage exposed shortcomings in ​its engineering systems and crisis response, according to internal memos reviewed by Reuters.

'Fog of ​war' Amanda Silver, Microsoft's corporate vice president overseeing M365 Core and Work IQ, the company's workplace intelligence platform for AI agents, said in a separate memo on Monday that engineers had to work through a "fog of war" as the outage unfolded.
In another memo earlier this month reviewed by ⁠Reuters, Henderson ​said "urgent patches to our M365 Core services" took too long to deploy worldwide.

stories.title: Govt cuts petrol by Re1, diesel by Rs4 for Nov 25
summary: The federal government on Tuesday decreased the price of petrol by Re1 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs4 per litre for November 25.
The latest revision comes a day after the government decreased the price of petrol by Rs3 per litre while keeping the price of HSD unchanged for November 24.
Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.

stories.title: Sales tax zones being established in Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad and Multan, PM told
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif was informed on Tuesday that separate sales tax zones were being established in the country’s four major taxpayer units — Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad and Multan — to improve collection.
According to a statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the development was shared during a weekly review meeting concerning the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) in Islamabad.
The statement released on Tuesday said that the meeting was also informed that work was underway to establish a modern cargo tracking system to address the sales tax gap and curb smuggling.

stories.title: COP collapse
summary: This omission was rejected by the EU, Britain, and some small, climate-vulnerable states, which rightly hold fossil fuels responsible for global warming.

Ironically, many of the countries that opposed the deal for not including the transition away from fossil fuels, refused to move forward on earlier pledges to provide and mobilise funding for poor climate-vulnerable countries.

It has been noted, in fact, that many of the latter prefer funds over curbs on fossil fuels at this stage, given their need to rehabilitate lives already impacted by climate change and build infrastructure strong enough to withstand future shocks.

stories.title: UN chief warns AI could fuel conflict, calls for urgent action on autonomous weapons
summary: Three major threats to international peace Guterres outlined three principal risks associated with the rapid development and deployment of artificial intelligence.

AI opportunities for peacekeeping and mediation Despite his warnings, Guterres emphasized that emerging technologies could make important contributions to international peace and security when developed and deployed responsibly.

Drawing comparisons with aviation, medicine, and nuclear energy, Guterres said public confidence in powerful technologies has depended on systems of oversight and accountability. “The same standard must apply to artificial intelligence,” he said.

stories.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill 7, including senior security official
summary: Israeli airstrikes in Gaza on Tuesday killed seven people, including Hamas’s director of internal security, Palestinian officials in the territory told AFP, despite a ceasefire in place since last year.
Police station strike Bassal said earlier on Tuesday that three people, including a 17-year-old, had been killed in a separate Israeli airstrike near Gaza City.
Israel’s military said it “struck terrorists in the area” of the police station, but did not confirm the strike that killed the 17-year-old.

stories.title: Freedom of speech should not become a shield for those crossing 'red lines', says Naqvi
summary: He alleged that only 47 per cent of the complaints made by the Counter Terrorism Department were acted upon by social media platforms. “This is not about technology, this is about people.
The minister called for moving from policy towards enforcement. “To begin with [social media] platforms, OTT services and major content creators must register with the authority.

Naqvi then went on to recount a recent town hall meeting, where he met five girls who were on the verge of ending their lives due to someone about to release “sensitive material” on social media platforms. “We don’t have any pathway for approaching those platforms.

stories.title: Eight killed, seven injured as passenger vehicle plunges into ravine in KP's Torghar
summary: At least eight people, including two women, were killed and seven others injured on Tuesday when a passenger vehicle plunged into a deep ravine in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Torghar district, Rescue 1122 said.
Earlier this month, three people were killed and 13 others injured when a coach collided with a motorcycle in Dera Ismail Khan.
Earlier in the month, at least eight people were also killed and 30 others injured when a passenger bus collided with a truck near the Havelian Interchange on Hazara Motorway.

stories.title: Balochistan announces rewards of up to Rs250m for information on most-wanted terrorists
summary: The Balochistan government has announced cash rewards ranging from Rs500,000 to Rs250 million for individuals providing credible information about the province's most-wanted terrorists.
The provincial government announced the rewards through an official advertisement, a copy of which was also shared on X by Babar Yousafzai, the chief minister's assistant on home affairs.
On November 13, security forces killed 74 terrorists during operations in Balochistan and Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa.

stories.title: Speakers call for social media accountability, balanced regulation to curb disinformation
summary: Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said Pakistan had nearly 100 million social media users and around 160 million smartphone users, making the spread of unverified information a major challenge.

He said the shift from traditional to social media had transformed the information landscape, allowing anyone with a smartphone to produce and disseminate content and making verification increasingly difficult.
Memon urged social media platforms to deploy artificial intelligence and other tools to identify harmful content, particularly material inciting violence.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz congratulates CDF Munir on Hall of Fame induction at Malaysia’s National Defence Studies Centre
summary: On Monday, ISPR said CDF Munir would also visit the National Defence Studies Centre, where a formal ceremony would be held to induct him as the 21st member of its “prestigious” Hall of Fame.
In a meeting with Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim on Monday, CDF Munir reaffirmed their shared commitment to strengthening bilateral defence ties in Putrajaya.
CDF Munir also held a meeting with Malaysian Defence Minister Mohamed Khaled bin Nordin.

stories.title: ‘The universe has no borders': Pakistan's historic space mission draws global praise
summary: Pakistan's first astronaut mission entered its final stages, with Muhammad Zeeshan Ali set to make history as the country's first astronaut to travel to China's Tiangong space station aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft.
Together, let's go further." Congratulations to Muhammad Zeeshan Ali from Pakistan for becoming the first foreign astronaut to board China's #Tiangong space station!

Pakistan is poised to send an astronaut into space for the first time on Wednesday, when air force pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali joins China’s Shenzhou-24 mission to the country’s Tiangong space station.
